seo.title: Danial Shabanian — Trustworthy autonomy for spinal surgery
seo.description: PhD researcher at Nottingham Trent University (MEDRG) building ScoliBot, a co-robotic system for spinal surgery with a trust-calibrated explanation layer.

hero.kicker: PhD Researcher · MEDRG, Nottingham Trent University
hero.headline: Teaching surgical robots to *explain* themselves.
hero.lede: A mechanical engineer turned robotics researcher. I build ScoliBot, a co-robotic system for spinal surgery, and the trust-calibrated explanation layer that lets surgeons see why the robot acts, and when to step in.

research.title: Robots a surgeon can *trust*, for the right reasons.

featured.title: ScoliBot
featured.body: A co-robotic system for spinal surgery, built for precision, safety and better surgeon–robot interaction, with a trust-calibrated explanation and supervision layer. A formalised LLM explanation pipeline turns the robot's internal state into plain-language reasons, so the team's trust tracks how reliable the robot really is.

projects.title: LLM explanation pipeline
projects.body: A formalised pipeline that grounds every explanation in the robot's real state, with an ablation study on what each stage adds.

projects.title: 3D FDM printer, designed and built
projects.body: As lab technician at the Advanced Material Behaviour Lab, led the design and construction of a fused-deposition 3D printer from scratch.

projects.title: Precise rotary desk
